H9003:
ב
ב, בּ, Bêth, 2nd letter; post Biblical Hebrew = numeral 2 (and so in margin of printed MT); ב֟ = 2000; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

I. בְּ, preposition in (Moabite בּ, Syriac …, Arabic …, Ethiopic …) before tone-syllables in certain cases (Ges§ 102. 2) בָּ, with suffix בִּי; בְּךָ (; ; בְּכָה), in pause and feminine בָּךְ; בּוֺ (once, Kt בֹּה), בָּהּ; בָּנוּ; בָּכֶם, [בָּכֶן]; בָּהֶם, בָּם [also בָּהֵ֫מָּה ; ; ], בָּהֶן ; ; [15 times בָּהֵן (FrMM 235), and thrice, ; ; , בָּהֵ֫נָּה]. Preposition denoting properly in, Greek ἐν, but applied in many derived and figurative significations. The senses expressed by בְּ are grouped by the Rabbis in three classes, בֵּית הַכְּלִי Beth vasculi, בֵּית הַדִּיבִּוּק וְהַנְּגִיעָה Beth coniunctionis et viciniae, בֵּית הָעֵזֶר Beth auxilii; and the same arrangement may be followed here, though the limits between the three classes are not clearly defined, and they sometimes overlap one another.
I. In:
1. strictly, of position in a place (which often is expressed more precisely by בְּקֶרֶב, בְּתוֺךְ), as בַּבַּיִת in the house, בָּעִיר in the city, בַּדּוּד in the pot, בָּאָרֶץ in the land, etc. constantly. Hebrew idiom also says בָּהָר in the mountain etc., even in cases where we could hardly avoid saying on, as ; : so בְּחֹרֵב and elsewhere; בְּראֹשׁ הָהָר ; . Preceded by a verb of motion (especially עָבַר) בְּ = through, as and Abram passed through בָּאָרֶץ in the land = passed through it, ; +; in (= through) a gate, ; ; . Figurative to speak בְּאָזְנֵי in the ears of ...; to be good (or evil, etc.) בְּעֵינֵי in the eyes of ...
2. of presence in the midst of a multitude, among, there was not left בָּהֶם among them even one, ; Ahitophel בַּקֹּשְׁרִים is among the conspirators, בְּכֹל מַלְכֵי יְהוּדָה. So בְּךָ in thee (of Israel, collective) ; ; ; ; ; (different from עִמָּ֑ח beside thee ). — Specifically
  a. of an individual, implying eminency among: ; Tabor among the mountains, ; ; הַיָּפָה בַנָּשִׁים the fair one (= the fairest) among women, : compare . On see Dr.
  b. hence with some verbs, when the action refers to only a part of the object, as הִכָּהַ בְּ to smite among... i.e. to smite some of... (different from הִכָּה with accusative); הָרַג בְּ נָשָׂא בְּ to bear in, i.e. to share in bearing, and elsewhere; בָּנָה בְּ to build in or at ; עָשָׂה בְּ עָמֵל בְּ to labour on אָכַל בְּ, שָׁתָה בְּ to eat or drink of ; חָלַק בְּ to give a share in .
  c. specifying the parts of which a whole consists (especially in P) ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; .
3. with reference to the limits enclosing a space, within: בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ within thy gates, בְּחוֺמוֺתַי within my walls.
4. often pregn. with verbs of motion, when the movement to a place results in rest in it, into: after בָּא ; נָתַן שָׁלַח to send in among ; ; . — (an extreme case) שׁוּב בְּ to return (and rest) in thy God, (unless לַזָּבַ֑ח should be read, as v). — עַיִן בְּעַיִן (with) eye (looking) into eye ; פָּנִים בְּפָנִים בְּ ׳עֵינֵי פְ the eyes of ... are upon, both in favourable (; ) and hostile (; ) sense.
5. applied to time, as בְּרֵאשִׁית in the beginning; בַּיּוֺם הַשְּׁבִיעִי on the seventh day; בַּשָּׁנָה הַהִיא in that year; & constantly.
6. of a state or condition, whether material or mental, in which an action takes place: so often, בְּשָׁלוֺם in peace בַּצָּרָה in distress הָלַךְ בְּתֻמּוֺ to walk in his integrity; בְּרָע in evil case.
7. בְּ introduces the predicate, denoting it as that in which the subject consists, or in which it shews itself (the Beth essentiae, — common in Arabic, especially with a participle or adjective and in a negative sentence: Qor 2:79 … and God (appears) not as one remiss; 2:7 … and they are not believers [compare French en — en honnête homme]; see WAG ii. § 56 a): namely
  a. a primary predicate, the God of my fathers בְּעֶזְרִי was my help, ; (read כִּי מִי בְעֶזְֶרךָ׃ with ᵐ5 ᵑ6 Che and others); בְּיָהּ שְׁמוֺ his name consists in Yah, ; . With the predicate in the plural (as plural of majesty) בְּעֹזְרָ֑י ׳י J. is my great helper, (see Che), .
  b. a secondary predicate, and I appeared unto them בְּאֵל שַׁדָּ֑י as God Almighty, בְּנַחֲלָה as an inheritance, ; ; ; ; I have not put away therefrom בְּטָמֵא as one unclean = while unclean, ; בְּחָזָק יָבוֺא he cometh as a strong one, (where see De) and rise up as my help, v, ; ; ; (De).
  c. a predicate as accusative, I have refined thee וְלֹא בְכָ֑סֶף but not as though silver, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; (twice in verse) (read יַפִּלוּ) (see ᵐ5 Co) all בְּנַחֲלָה (compare
  b.), & allotted it בְּחֶבֶל נַחֲלָה as a line of inheritance (i.e. as a measured inheritance). ׳כִּי בְּיָהּ יהוה צוּר עוֺלָמִים י is different — for in Yah there is a rock of ages (compare Qor 4:7; 4:47 there is sufficiency in God as a patron).
  d. in comparisons, consume away בֶּעָשָׁן in the form of, as, smoke ; ; ; .
II. Denoting proximity —
1. at, by (not very common): בָּעַיִן by the spring; ; בִּנְהַר כְּבָר by the river Chebar ( עַל).
2. on: ; בַּמִּזְבֵּחַ on the altar; on the necks of the camels; and elsewhere בְּמָתְנָיו on his loins; a helmet בְּראֹשׁוֺ on his head.
3. often with verbs of touching, approaching, taking hold of, cleaving, etc., as אָחַז, דָּבֵק, חָשַׁק, נָגַע, נָגַשׁ, קָרַב, פָּגַּע, תָּמַךְ, תָּפַשׂ (see these words).
4. with words expressing or implying an act of hostility —
  a. against: יָדוֺ בַכֹּל וְיַד כֹּל בּוֺ his hand against all, and the hand of all against him; בּ ׳הָֽיְתָה יַד פְּ ; ; + often Hence after verbs (q. v.) of fighting (נִלְחַם, רִיב), going up to invade (עָלָה), being angry (הִתְעַבֵּר, אָנַף, חָרָה אַף), sinning or acting treacherously (חָטָא, בָּגַד, מָרַד, מָרָה, מָעַל, פָּשַׁע, שִׁקֵּר, כִּזֵּב, כִּחֵשׁ), testifying (עָנָה, הֵעִיד), mocking (הִלְעִיג, הֵתֵל), feeling loathing (קוּץ), rebuking (גָּעַר: properly to protest loudly), speaking (דִּבֶּר: b), etc., & even (an extreme case) יָסוּרוּ בִי they turn aside (so as to be) against me. In a weaker sense מַשְׁתִּין בַּקִּיר mingens ad parietem and elsewhere
  b. down to, upon (super with accusative), especially in such phrases as דָּמָיו בּוֺ and elsewhere his blood be upon him; דָּמוֺ בְראֹשׁוֺ his blood be upon his head ) בְּראֹשׁוֺ׳שׁוּב (הֵשִׁיב י (רָעָה), (דָּם), v (רָעָה), (עֲמָלוֺ); ׳בְּראֹשׁוֺ נָתַן דֶּרֶךְ פּ & often in Ezekiel, as ; .
III. 1. With —
  a. of accompaniment: בְּעַם כָּבֵד with much people, ; ; ; ; ; and he shall give בִּפְלִלִים with arbitrators (arbitrators being employed), בְּלִמֻּדָֽי׃ with my disciples, i.e. having them present; ; ; עֵץ בְּלַחְמוֺ a tree with its sap; וְהוּא בִּשְׁנֵים הֶעָשָׂר and he with the 12th.
  b. often of what one takes or brings with one: בְּמַקְלִי with my staff I passed over Jordan, ; ; ; ; and elsewhere קִדֵּם בְּ to go to meet with; בָּא בְּ to come with ; ; . (In Arabic this usage is developed more fully than in Hebrew, and … literally to come with, … literally to go away with, are used idiomatically in the sense of to bring, and to take away respectively: WAG ii. § 56 b.) Hence בְּאֵין, בְּאֶפֶס, בִּבְלִי, בְּלֹא = without.
  c. of concomitant (or surrounding) conditions, as בְּחִפָּזוֺן with (or in) haste; בְּצֶדֶק with (or in) righteousness; בִּשְׁגָגָה in error; בִּתְרוּעָה וּבְקוֺל שׁוֺפָר often in such phrases as בְּצִדְקָֽתְךָ in thy righteousness; בְּחַסְדְּךָ in thy mercy — בְּאָשְׁרִי with my happiness! = happy am I ; the voice of ׳י is בַּכֹּחַ with power = is powerful; בְּרָעָה with evil purpose; בְרָע in wickedness; בִּגְבוּרֹת with strength.
2. of the instrument or means: as
  a. בַּחֶרֶב with the sword etc.; בְּרַגְלַיִם with the feet . . . בְּיַד by the hand of ... (see below יָד); to stone בְּאֶבֶן or בָּֽאֲבָנִים with stones ; etc.; שָׁתָה בְּ to drink with a cup ; (compare in Aramaic ); to cry בְּגָרוֺן with the throat to burn בָּאֵשׁ in or with fire (often); to slay or to perish בָּרָעָב through hunger or בַּדֶּבֶר through pestilence ; + often (compare בַּמָּוֶת יִקָּבֵ֑רוּ); to save with or by ; .
  b. idiomatic, with certain verbs, as שָׁחַק בְּ to play with עָבַד בְּ to labour with a person (as with an instrument), i.e. to use him as a slave ; ; and elsewhere; עָשָׂה בְּ ; ; ; ; ; ; & perhaps דִּבֶּר בְּ (of God) to speak with one ; a and elsewhere (see Ew§ 217 f. (3); DrSm ii. 23, 2). Further בַּבַּעַל, הִתְנַבֵּא ביהוה to prophesy with or by ׳י or Baal, ׳י or Baal being the inspirer; שָׁאַל בְּ, דָּרַשׁ to inquire or ask by means of a god (or oracle).
  c. ביהוה through ׳י (= by His aid) in many connections, as ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; with passive verbs ; (to be saved): and even of the immediate cause to be commanded ביהוה by ׳י, בָּאָדָם by man shall his blood be shed (both unusual), .

(i.e. the name being used or appealed to in the act) ; , etc. (so to swear ביהוה by ׳י etc.,בִּימִינוֺ to bless בְּךָ with thee , to swear with me , i.e. using my name in oath, ); almost = in the authority and power of ; ; ; ; ; ; ; .

3. of cost or price (the Beth pretii), the price, whether given or received, being treated as the instrumental means by which the act is accomplished, with, for, at the cost of: thus regularly
  a. with שָׂכַר hire , פָּדָה redeem , אֵרֵשׂ betroth , קָנָה buy ; בְּנַפְשׁוֺ at the cost of his life hath A. spoken this word, who went בְּנַפְשׂוֺתָם at peril of their lives, ; ; בִּבְכֹרוֺ יְיַסְּדֶנָּה at the price of his firstborn shall he lay its foundations, בְּרָאשֵׁינוּ to the jeopardy of our heads he will fall away, etc.
  b. with מָכַר sell עָבַד serve ; ; הֵמִיר exchange ; their glory I will exchange for ignominy, נָתַן בְּנֶשֶׁךְ to give for interest ; in other connections ; f.; ; ; ; ; נֶפֶשׁ בְּנֶפֶשׁ עַיִן בְּעַיִן life for life, eye for eye; בַּמֶּה נֶחְשָׁב הוּא at what is he to be accounted? a thousand vines בְּאֶלֶף כָּ֑סֶף at a thousand (shekels of) silver. — Hence (perhaps) the idiomatic usages שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה year for year, one year like another, annually and elsewhere; יוֺם בְּיוֺם (late), כְּיוֺם בְּיוֺם כְּפַעַם בְּפַעַם (see יוֺם, פַּעַם); חֹדֶשׁ בְּחֹדֶשׁ .
4. rather peculiarly, in certain cases where the object of an action may be treated as the instrument by which it is accomplished: as הֵנַיעַ בְּראֹשׁ to shake with the head ; (as well as הֵנִיעַ ראֹשׁ ); to open with the mouth , with the lips to gnash with the teeth (to gnash the teeth ); to wink with the eye (to wink the eye, ib. ); נָתַן בְּקוֺל to utter with the voice ; ; (but נָתַן קוֺל is more common); to stretch out with the hand הֵרִים בַּמַּטֶּה (unusual) . 6. of the material with which a work is wrought, both absolute עָשָׁה בַזָּהָב to work with gold ; and to make a thing with (in our idiom, of) gold ; ; (בָּנָה). Without a verb ; .

IV. בְּ is used also with certain classes of verbs, though the explanation of its use may be sometimes doubtful: namely
  a. with verbs of taking refuge, trusting, relying, as הֶאֱמִין, בָּטַח, חָסָה, נִשְׁעַן.
  b. with verbs of ruling, governing, restraining, as מָלַךְ, מָשַׁל, נָגַשׂ, עָצַר, רָדָה, שָׁלַט.
  c. with verbs of rejoicing, feeling pleasure or satisfaction, etc., as גִּיל, עָלַץ, שׂוּשׂ, שָׂמֵחַ, חָפֵץ, רָצָה, שָׂבַע (but with this verb מִן is more common). [Probably a case of
III. 5.]
  d. with verbs expressive of sensible perception, to denote the pleasurable or attentive exercise of the faculty concerned, as שָׁמַע בְּ to listen to, הִבִּיט בְּ, רָאָה, חָזָה, to look upon, הֵרִיחַ בְּ to smell at (see these words).
  e. occasionally also with verbs of speaking, thinking, mentioning, knowing, to denote the object of the action, as דִּבֶּר בְּ to speak about ; and elsewhere (see below דִּבֶּר); הִלֵּל בְּ, הָגָה, שִׂיחַ ; ; יָדַע זָכַר once , הִזְכִּיר often; בְּךָ תְהִלָּתִי of thee is my praise.
V. Followed by an infinitive with, בְּ forms a periphrasis for the gerund, though in English it is commonly to be rendered by a verb and conjunction, namely: —
1. as a temporal conjunction, as בְּהִבָּֽרְאָם in their being created = when they were created, בִּהְיוֺתָם in their being (= when they were) in the field; and constantly. Sometimes it has in appearance the force of after that, as ; ; but as a rule this is really due to the action denoted by the infinitive being treated as extending over a period within which the action of the principal verb takes place: so especially in the phrase בְּצֵאת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרַיִם, even of events at the close of the 40 years, ; ; , the whole period being treated as that in which Egypt was left (compare , where the time included is future). Cases, however, occur in which this explanation will hardly apply, as ; .
2. as a causal conjunction (compare above III. 5), as ׳בְּחֶמְלַת י עָלָיו through J.'s having compassion upon him, ; ; ; אֹתָנוּ ׳בְּשִׂנְאַת י through J.'s hating us, etc. ( similarly מִן), (= in that ye have ...) ; ; ; .
3. as a concessive conjunction, when = though: ; בְּהָמִיר אָ֑רֶץ though the earth do change.
Note. — בָּאַרְבֶּה can only be rendered 'with the locusts,' the locusts being conceived as implicit in Moses' uplifted hand: but probably לָאַרְבֶּה should be read. Thrice in late Hebrew בְּ is used peculiarly: for with misfortune was it in his house (בְּרָעָה chosen for the purpose of explaining בְּרִיעָה); עֲלֵיהֶם בַּמְּלָאכָה it devolved upon them with the work; for with terror (was it) upon them from the peoples of the countries (the sentence without a verb as often in Chronicles: DrIntr. 504 f.): compare . compare Ew§ 295 f.

ה, He, fifth letter; = numeral 5 in post-Biblical Hebrew; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

הַּ , הַ, הָ, הֶ (on the use of these different forms, see the Grammars: e.g. Ges§ 35), definite article, the (so Moabite, Phoenician (Schröd§ 62-4), Liµyan (Northwest Arabia) ha (DHMEpigr. Denkm. 4. 13. 58 ff.); not Assyrian Aramaic or Ethiopic: Arabic …, of which, before dentals, sibilants, and liquids, the l is written but not pronounced, thus … pronounced 'ash-shamsu = Hebrew הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ) — in general the use of the article in Hebrew is analogous to its use in Greek or German: but naturally there are applications peculiar to Hebrew (compare with what follows Ges§ 126 Ew§ 277): —
1. joined with substantives:
  a. to mark a definite concrete object, as the heavens and the earth, הַמֶּלֶךְ the king, etc. Never, however (as in Greek e.g. ὁ Πλάτων), before true proper names, though it is used with certain terms, chiefly geographical, of which the original appellative sense has not been lost, as הַבַּעַל 'Baal,' literally 'the lord,' in plural הַבְּעָלִים i.e. the various local Baals, הַשָּׂטָן the Adversary ff.   c. with nouns which are not definite in themselves, but acquire their definition from the context, or from the manner in which they are introduced: thus (α) in the standing phrases הַיּוֺם to-day, ; + often; הַלַּיְלָה to-night, ; +, once last night; so הַשָּׁנָה this year, ; הַפַּעַם this time, +.   d. it is a peculiarity of Hebrew thought to conceive an object as defined by its being taken for a particular purpose, and thus by a kind of prolepsis to prefix the article to the noun denoting it: and Samuel took אֶתפַּֿךְ הַשֶּׁמֶן literally the cruse of oil, not, however, a cruse which had been defined previously, but one rendered definiteby being now taken; in English idiom 'a cruse of oil,' v בַּסֵּפֶר literally in the scroll or book, the one, namely taken for the purpose, i.e. in a scroll (so ; ; ), בַּשִּׂמְלָה, וַתְּכַסֵּהוּ בַּשְּׂמִיכָה, v; הָאֹהֶל a tent, ; אֶתהַֿקַּרְדֻּמֹּת hatchets, every one able to sling בָּאֶבֶן אֶלהַֿשַּׂעֲרָה with a stone at a hair, בָּאַרְגָּז (unless indeed the אַרְגָּז was an understood appendage in every cart), הַנַּעַר, a young man, בַּמּוֺט on a pole, בַּחֶבֶל with a cord, השׁפחה a girl (compare Dr; ).   c. it is used in questions which, by seeming to make doubtful what cannot be denied, have the force of an impassioned or indignant affirmation: ('dubitantis speciem prae se fert Esavus, ut eo acerbius affirmet,' Maurer, cited by Ges), הֲנִגְלהֹ נִגְלֵיתִי וגי Did I reveal myself to the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt ? etc. (i.e. of course I did, although thy sons, by their actions, appear to belie it), (expressing astonishment), הֲרָצַחְתָּ וְגַםיָֿרָ֑שְׁתָּ Hast thou slain, and also taken possession ? ; ; (compare Hi); also , and the phrases הַרְּאִיתֶם do ye see ? ; הֲרָאִיתָ dost thou see ? ; ; ; and elsewhere
